author: vdplet
body:
AUTHOR HOLD — Smith directly requested in the VDPlet chat: 'send recommendations to rally on how to improve timing. it is not to begin any work until i follow up with it.' This delivery is advisory only. Read/retain it, then wait for Smith's direct follow-up. Do not begin a new plan, instrumentation, source change, build, test, benchmark, reservation, emulator/hardware action or next tranche from these recommendations. No acknowledgement-only reply is requested.

I examined your retained NAT-002 results and exact guest/native sources read-only. The complete-frame negative result stands. My earlier emphasis on lease traffic is weaker; the result does not separately time native physics or prove that checks are free. Detailed findings: /Agon/mystuff/agon-vdplet/docs/tasks/VDPL-024/RALLY-NAT002-FOLLOWUP.md; derived retained timestamp/phase analysis and input hashes: /Agon/mystuff/agon-vdplet/docs/tasks/VDPL-024/rally-nat002-retained-timing-analysis.json.

Evidence worth carrying into any later selected timing plan:
1. Every one of5400 full-run frame differences is exactly TWO MOS ticks; PRT intervals vary21..41nominalms, medians25/26. MOS60 therefore discriminates no spare capacity in this cohort. Investigate clock/presentation coupling before interpreting that conversion; this observation alone does not prove its mechanism.
2. Guest player/rules/Tick time encloses eZ80 work and silent submissions, not native Tick execution. Its sends also enter sendMs. Those buckets overlap and cannot be summed into an exclusive frame partition. Reply waits mix queued physics, Render and post-swap reads.
3. State-only retains1374logical compatibility-export bytes/frame; coarse492, excluding metadata/completion. Root57globals198B plus five arrays96B are still serialized. Road, actor sampling, three drawing-list calls, HUD/sky and swap stay unchanged. Seven outbound bytes/frame are saved by coarse calls, not four synchronous round trips.

Recommendations ONLY AFTER Smith separately releases work:
TIM-01: Define separate complete-presented-frame latency/throughput, native operation intervals, guest computation, transmit and wait observables. Name each clock, unit, calibration, core and wrap rule. Preserve raw records. Do not label nominal CCOUNT conversion as independently measured physical time or PRT as calibrated emulator wall time. Whole-process time includes startup/teardown.
TIM-02: Time native Tick arithmetic separately from entry validation, input/import, compatible state exports and total RUN. For Render distinguish preflight/asset checks, row BEGIN/queued Canvas drain, row acquisition, road generation/stores, actor geometry/sampling, command generation/publication and total RUN. Show inclusive/nested intervals explicitly; same-core CCOUNT includes interrupts/preemption. Existing bounded native reads and caller storage/services should suffice, without a new timer ABI.
TIM-03: Keep ordinary Canvas execution and swap/presentation waiting separate from native renderer work. Retain outer guest submit-through-completion and post-swap fence boundaries. Do not interpret the present mixed wait bin as road time.
TIM-04: Make guest accounting nonoverlapping where feasible, or retain an explicit nesting/overlap map. Include traffic overrides, rank/audio/input work and boundary costs instead of assigning the subtraction residual to a fictional phase.
TIM-05: Preserve an uninstrumented exact baseline/control, bounded post-timing result export and a measured observer-overhead control. Avoid logging/UART output inside timed work. Keep exact workload/state/road/actor/command/sync/lifecycle oracles and frozen source/runtime/compiler policy. Any lighter production export protocol is a separately selected experiment, not a silent weakening of this comparison.
TIM-06: Separate fixed-pose/kernel attribution from full-race presentation throughput. The prepared same-byte hardware cohort can establish physical end-to-end timing when separately released; it does not automatically isolate a renderer cost. Report paired orders, raw distributions and uncertainty; do not discard slow runs or rerun for a desired gain.

VDPlet can review clock/ABI interpretation when Smith follows up. Rally retains consumer/source ownership. The recommendations select no runtime change or hardware deployment. Explicit hold remains: DO NOT BEGIN WORK UNTIL SMITH FOLLOWS UP WITH YOU.
